youtube.title: Her Father Gave the Ganga to the Gods | Ramayana Ep 10
youtube.description:
The Ganga and Goddess Uma were sisters. 🌊

On the bank of the Ganga, at Rama's asking, Vishvamitra began the tale of her birth. Himavan, lord of the mountains, had two daughters of matchless beauty. Their mother was Mena, Meru's daughter and Himavan's dear queen; the Ganga was the elder, and Uma the second. Then all the gods came and asked the mountain king for his elder daughter. And Himavan, true to dharma, gave her away for the good of the three worlds. Glad at heart, the gods carried the Ganga up to heaven. Her sister Uma took a stern vow and made austerity her wealth, and Himavan gave her in marriage to Rudra, the peerless one. These, said the sage, are the mountain king's two daughters: the Ganga, best of rivers, and the Goddess Uma. So the river of three paths went first to the sky, rising to the world of the gods.

📜 On screen (Valmiki Ramayana 1.35.18, vulgate):
"Dadau dharmeṇa himavāṃs tanayāṃ lokapāvanīm, svacchandapathagāṃ gaṅgāṃ trailokyahitakāmyayā"
(By dharma, wishing the good of the three worlds, Himavan gave his daughter, the Ganga, purifier of the worlds, who flows where she wills.)
